blurb: Projects in the home. The Store's engine and machine come from the Store.
reasons: Why hide_path: an agent meeting remove_file cold will use it like file.rm, and hide a path from the project's whole history.
Why stats has no commit: the caller named the Branch or --at; the Commit it counted is in the long form.

Why the list's stats are a size only: main's head already records its length, so project list --with stats costs one record per project. A file count is in no record: it needs a format change, or a tree walk that comes back partial for any repo with node_modules. project stats does that walk for one project and says partial; project get takes no --with.
Why file_count, not files: a plural noun is always a list, so a number is never named with one.
Why only a project has two doctor depths: the shallow check reads records; --full reads the data its Branches reach, which can take minutes.

calls.new_work: `state` and its companions (`op`, `blocked_by`, `reason`, `fix`) are new: a project has no state today, and its record holds no `op`. `blocked` comes from the records of its Store and that Store's machine, with no probe. `busy` needs an `op` in the project's record, as machines, Stores and Sandboxes keep one: `project.init` writes its record in its last phase today, so a project being imported is on no list, and `project.delete` keeps only its intent file (`store/<store>/delete/<project>.json`: pending, marked, done), which names no owner. `broken` with `unresolved` is a delete whose owner is gone while its intent is still pending and the Store still lists the project: today such a project is listed like any other, and calls that need its admission are refused `Unresolved` until `project delete` is run again. Listing the projects of a Store that cannot be opened is new: today an all-Stores listing leaves that Store out and a named one is refused. `commit` (main's head) per row is new in the answer: the listing already reads each project's stack record, which holds it, but keeps only the name and stack id, and the worker's listing reply does not carry it. `--with stats` is new: no call lists a size per project today. `size` is the length main's head Layer records (today's `logical`), one record read per project and no tree walk. It carries no file count: no record holds one, so it would need a format change; `project.stats` counts by a bounded walk. `--cursor` is new: today the call pages by position (`page_size`, `page_pos`, default 50). The cursor carries the call's filters only, and no Commit; one given with other filters, or to another call, is refused `InvalidInput`.

calls.note: shallow: its record (project.record) and its record against the Store's own list (project.listed); --full also reads everything reachable from main's head and each Branch's head (project.data). A project on record that the Store does not list is a notice with the fix layerfs project delete <project>, not an error. A not_checked entry carries blocked_by or reason (timeout, busy, lost). The answer is the one doctor shape; the project node's coverage is shallow, full with --full, or none when it could not be checked. checks is the project kind's whole list, in the order they run; store doctor runs the same list without the full-only entry on each of its projects. --full writes nothing to the Store: it may keep its visited set in a scratch file outside the Store, removed when the call ends, as today's integrity scan does. No check id of today's doctors names a project: the home sweep reads each project's record and folder, which project.record covers

calls.new_work: The call and its answer shape are new. The record check is not: `project.get` and `project.list` already compare a project's record with the Store's own list (and hide a project the Store does not list); the doctor reports that case as a notice with a fix. `--full` is new work: a streamed, bounded-memory walk of everything reachable from main's head and the head of each Branch, on both engines and through a machine's worker; today's integrity check has no scope smaller than a Store. It writes nothing to the Store; its visited set may live in a scratch file outside the Store, as today's integrity scan keeps its own in a private SQLite temporary database that is removed when the scan's connection closes. Progress events are new. The fix `layerfs project delete <project>` finishes a delete that kept the home's entry; no call today removes the entry of a project that was deleted from another home.
